Current presentation includes symptoms consistent with hypercalcemia (weakness, anorexia, nausea, constipation) and restless leg syndrome.

report.source_text: Given the threat of hypercalcemia crises, continuous renal replacement therapy(CRRT) with low calcium dialysate(Ca2+ 1.25 mmol/l) was applied instantly. Meanwhile, calcitriol pulse therapy was ceased while higher-dose cinacalcet(50 mg per day) was reused again. In addition, calcitonin was subcutaneously injected at a dose of 50u per day to lower the blood calcium, but poor response was achieved, and the serum albumin corrected calcium kept elevating to 3.77 mmol/l. Therefore, hormone therapy(intravenous injection of 40 mg methylprednisolone for 7 day, and oral administration of 20 mg prednisone until operation) was considered.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 70-year-old Chinese man with 2 years of hemodialysis for renal failure developed secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT) with PTH elevation from 100.3 pmol/L (December 2016) to 197.3 pmol/L despite cinacalcet therapy with poor compliance. He presented with hypercalcemic crisis characterized by albumin-corrected calcium of 3.96 mmol/L, elevated alkaline phosphatase (160 U/L), and symptoms including restless leg syndrome, anorexia, nausea, constipation, weakness, and sleep disturbance. Parathyroid ultrasound was normal. Despite intensive medical management (CRRT with low calcium dialysate, high-dose cinacalcet 50 mg/day, calcitonin 50 U/day, and corticosteroids), calcium remained elevated at 3.77 mmol/L. Parathyroidectomy was performed, revealing a 2 cm well-encapsulated mass with solid and cystic components. Post-operative response was excellent: calcium normalized to 2.12 mmol/L and PTH dropped to 21.41 pmol/L within 10 days, sustained at 3 months (calcium 2.30 mmol/L, PTH 18.63 pmol/L). The patient became free from restless leg syndrome and gastrointestinal distress. The progression from SHPT to tertiary HPT is evidenced by persistent hypercalcemia and elevated PTH despite medical therapy, with the characteristic set-point shift (elevated PTH despite high serum calcium).

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient had secondary hyperparathyroidism on hemodialysis with progressive PTH elevation despite medical therapy
At admission with hypercalcemic crisis: albumin-corrected calcium 3.96 mmol/L, ALP 160 U/L (elevated)
Parathyroid ultrasound on admission showed no abnormality

Medical management included CRRT with low calcium dialysate, high-dose cinacalcet 50 mg/day, calcitonin 50 U/day, and corticosteroids (methylprednisolone 40 mg IV × 7 days, then prednisone 20 mg oral)
Poor response to medical therapy with calcium remaining elevated at 3.77 mmol/L despite intensive treatment
Parathyroidectomy was performed with pathology revealing a 2 cm well-encapsulated mass with solid and cystic components
Post-operative response: calcium dropped to 2.12 mmol/L and PTH to 21.41 pmol/L within 10 days, sustained at 3 months (calcium 2.30 mmol/L, PTH 18.63 pmol/L)
Patient became free from restless leg syndrome and gastrointestinal distress within 3 months after surgery
Phosphorus level dropped to 1.77 mmol/L post-operatively

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Patient has renal failure on hemodialysis with documented secondary hyperparathyroidism; progression occurred in the context of chronic kidney disease and hemodialysis, not primary parathyroid disease

Parathyroid ultrasound normal; pathology showed benign parathyroid tissue (well-encapsulated mass with solid and cystic components); excellent response to parathyroidectomy with normalization of calcium and PTH

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.alternative: Vitamin D intoxication or granulomatous disease
ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Clinical context of renal failure and hemodialysis; calcitriol pulse therapy was ceased; pathology confirmed parathyroid origin of hypercalcemia

remaining_uncertainties: Serum PTH level at the time of admission with hypercalcemic crisis (before parathyroidectomy) - would directly document the set-point shift characteristic of tertiary HPT (elevated PTH despite high serum calcium of 3.96 mmol/L)
Serum phosphate level at admission - would complete the mineral metabolism profile at presentation
Operative findings details (which parathyroid glands were removed, extent of resection, intraoperative findings) - would clarify the surgical approach and extent of parathyroid pathology
